output_document.summary: The API validation rule has been updated based on lessons learned from a Q3 2024 rate limit incident. The new validation requirements mandate: (1) all limit changes require 72-hour advance notice to API consumers, (2) clients must have a documented escalation path, and (3) rate limit headers must be included in all API responses. These changes address the previous incident where consumers received only 24 hours notice before the rate limit was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute, causing 2-4 hour outages. This decision is classified as internal and applies to the default project.

The API validation rule decision has been recorded in the project store with internal classification. The decision captures three key requirements implemented to prevent future incidents like the Q3 2024 rate limit incident: mandatory 72-hour advance notice for all rate limit changes (versus the previous 24-hour notice that caused outages), establishment of documented escalation paths for API consumers, and inclusion of rate limit headers in all API responses. These changes directly address the root causes of the incident that resulted in 2-4 hour outages when the rate limit was reduced from 1000 to 500 requests per minute.
